text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: To advance our goal of building effective packages and enriching tabs, we should prioritize creating user-friendly templates that streamline the drafting process, labeling each one as 'Created by EXCAVA.' This approach will enhance consistency across our outputs and make it easier for creators to produce high-quality work efficiently. The trade-off we're accepting here is the initial development time required to create these templates, which may delay other tasks in the short term, but ultimately will lead to a faster and more coherent workflow in the long run.

name: Vet
text: I'm not convinced that prioritizing user-friendly templates is the best approach, as it may overlook the potential complexity of our packages and tabs, which could lead to oversimplification and limitations in our drafting process. A better alternative might be to focus on developing a flexible framework that can adapt to diverse creator needs, allowing for more nuanced and detailed outputs. To settle this argument, I'd like to see a comparison of the two approaches, with specific examples of how they would handle complex package and tab scenarios.
